items.title: WHO and ADVANCE-ID strengthen clinical trial capacity through workshop
items.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Advancing Clinical Evidence in Infectious Diseases (ADVANCE-ID) Network jointly organised the ADVANCE-ID Clinical Trial Workshop 2026, held from 31 August to 2 September 2026 in Singapore. The workshop contributed to wider capacity-strengthening efforts through the Global Clinical Trials Forum (GCTF), bringing together researchers from different regions to strengthen practical skills in the design and conduct of high-quality clinical trials.ADVANCE-ID

items.title: Early menopause: Why better research and global guidance matter for women’s health
items.summary: Physician and scientist Priya Satalkar-Götz experienced her first symptoms of menopause in her mid-twenties, but it took several years for her to receive a diagnosis. In this conversation, she reflects on the physical and personal impact of early menopause, the limits of medical knowledge without strong evidence and how greater investment in research and global guidance could transform care for future generations. items.title: INTERPOL and WHO sign agreement to strengthen global health and security protection
items.summary: INTERPOL and the World Health Organization (WHO) have signed a cooperation agreement aimed at tackling some of the most pressing threats at the intersection of public health and security.

items.title: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus - Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Between 1 January and 5 October 2026, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia reported eight laboratory-confirmed cases of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) infection, including one death. Cases were detected across six locations: Al Jouf (1), Arar (1), Hafr Al-Batin (1), Riyadh (2), Tabuk (1) and Taif (2). No epidemiological links were identified between any of the cases. items.title: Requests for inclusion of new neglected tropical diseases put on hold pending review of criteria
items.summary: The Strategic and Technical Advisory Group for Neglected Tropical Diseases (STAG-NTD) has recommended a temporary pause in the consideration of requests to add new diseases to the World Health Organization (WHO) list of neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), pending a comprehensive review of the criteria and processes used to determine inclusion.

items.title: Countries move to accelerate action against lead poisoning
items.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) is calling on countries to accelerate action to prevent lead exposure, a widespread but preventable health threat estimated to contribute to more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year and affecting hundreds of millions of children.

items.title: WHO formalize partnership with the largest organization for physicians and oncology professionals
items.summary: WHO and the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) have signed a collaboration agreement with the joint objective of elevating quality as a priority in the global cancer agenda and supporting governments in implementing programmes that improve access and, ultimately, survival.

items.title: WHO Guideline Development Group meets to review Abortion care guideline
items.summary: The World Health Organization has transitioned the Abortion care guideline to a living guideline format to focus on targeted recommendations that address new evidence or implementation issues as they arise. To this effect, the evidence for repeat dosing for the misoprostol-alone regimen for medical abortion at less than 12 weeks will be revisited (Recommendation 27b). items.title: WHO and partners drive improved alignment for effective NTD and supply chain delivery
items.summary: The meetings – the NTD Supply Chain Forum (NTD-SCF), the Supply Chain Technical Support Mechanism (SCTSM) and the Global Coordination and Stewardship Committee (GCSC) – brought together global, regional and national stakeholders to review progress, address persistent supply chain challenges and consider how NTD programmes can prepare for the changing environment toward and beyond 2030.

items.title: WHO launches TB in pregnancy and lactation research toolkit
items.summary: WHO has launched the TB in pregnancy and lactation research toolkit, a new online resource designed to support the earlier and optimal inclusion of pregnant and lactating women in tuberculosis (TB) research. The toolkit provides practical guidance and tools for researchers, trial sponsors, ethics committees, regulators and other stakeholders involved in TB drug and vaccine research.

items.title: WHO invites organizations worldwide to join the Together for Science and Health movement
items.summary: a global call inviting organizations and institutions to affiliate with Together for Science and Health, a new movement to strengthen the connection between science, health and society and build trust in evidence-informed decision-making.

items.title: WHO welcomes adoption of United Nations political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response
items.summary: The Political Declaration on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response provides a strong reaffirmation of the global solidarity and commitment needed to protect future generations from the devastating impacts of pandemics.

items.title: IPC Sudan Food Insecurity and Malnutrition Alert
items.summary: The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), of which WHO is a member, today issued a Food Insecurity and Malnutrition Alert for Sudan.

items.title: WHO Pandemic Hub sets ambitious goal to detect new outbreaks within 24 hours
items.summary: WHO launched a new five-year strategy for its Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, charting a path towards a world where every country can detect and understand emerging health threats within 24 hours of their appearance by 2030.

items.title: Pneumonia of undetermined etiology - the Russian Federation
items.summary: On 2 October 2026, WHO became aware through media reports of the death of an employee of the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute (APRI) of Siberia and the Far East, the Russian Federation. According to these reports, the individual died on 2 October following hospitalization for severe pneumonia on 29 September, and pneumonic plague was suspected as the cause of death, following occupational exposure in laboratory settings. items.title: WHO Youth Council welcomes 2026–2028 members in Berlin
items.summary: The WHO Youth Council launched its 2026–2028 term in Berlin on 9–10 October 2026, bringing together 25 youth-led and youth-serving organizations from around the world. Members reviewed progress from the previous term, set priorities for the next two years, and strengthened their role in advancing meaningful youth participation in global health governance. The meeting was followed by participation in the World Health Summit.

items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: On 5 October 2026, WHO was informed about a laboratory-confirmed imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Kenya with travel history from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The patient travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to Kenya through Uganda. The patient was hospitalized and treated in Kenya but subsequently died on 5 October. items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 11 September 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded further, with two additional health zones affected. items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 28 August 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded to one additional health zone, Kayna, in North Kivu. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is in a phase of intense transmission. It is the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in the country and expanding faster than any previous Ebola outbreak. The epidemic is increasingly characterized by sustained transmission within interconnected geographic clusters. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is intensifying, with sustained transmission and continued increases in reported cases and deaths. Initially confined to the Mongbwalu health zone in Ituri Province, over the last two months, the outbreak has expanded to five provinces (Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo), now affecting 49 health zones. items.summary: The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains active, with sustained transmission driving increases in reported cases and deaths. As of 15 July 2026, a cumulative total of 2124 confirmed cases, including 828 deaths, have been reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
